sources.author: Ashesh Rambachan, Jonathan Roth and contributors

inspected_anchors.finding: Version 0.2.8; R>=3.6; CVXR>=1.8, ECOSolveR, Rglpk and other imports; MIT + file LICENSE.
Holder/year notice; full grant is separately saved in LICENSE.md.
Complete MIT grant, copyright/notice retention and warranty disclaimer.
CVXR interface compatibility repairs in 0.2.7/0.2.8 and options-test addition; no support SLA.
Smoothness interface defaults FLCI and first post-period; data-dependent default M grid uses hardcoded .05 for multi-preperiod calibration.
Selected serial and parallel conditional smoothness paths reduce accepted grid to min/max endpoints.
FLCI warns that the requested sign restriction is unused.
FLCI warns that the requested shape restriction is unused.
Relative-magnitude interface defaults C-LF, ten Mbar values on[0,2], 1000 inference grid points; serial path reduces accepted grid to endpoints.
Original interval uses requested post-period contrast and its covariance, without robust trend adjustment.
Nonconformability refuses; asymmetry and negative covariance eigenvalues warn without a corrective projection.
Second differences and removal of normalized baseline construct smoothness restrictions.
LP target extrema; both nonzero statuses yield unadjusted point target with warning; one-failure branch not separately guarded here.
First-difference relative-magnitude restrictions indexed by maximum preperiod direction and sign.
Component LP extrema; both failed statuses yield point target without local warning; outer bounds use global min/max; comment assumes nonnegative target weights.
Single-post conditional path delegates to no-nuisance inversion; multi-post path to nuisance inversion. Delegates not fully reviewed.
Low-level default1000; grid bounds +/-20 post-target SE around zero; union membership retained across signed components.

supported_claims: RM and SD use first and second differences with different tuning units and different zero-tuning assumptions.
Defaults and retained numerical information differ between high-level, low-level and did bridge entrypoints.
Warnings, accepted-grid membership and solver status must accompany any sensitivity result.
Failed LP status can reach a point-target fallback; source reachability is not an observed package failure.

Repository revision declares 0.2.8; equivalence to release-tag, CRAN or installed binary bytes is unverified.
Full top-level MIT terms inspected; solver, transitive dependency, redistribution and deployment review remains open.
No complete inspection of all conditional inversion, CVXR, sign/shape, parallel or solver-status branches.
Gaussian projection is an authored conservative oracle under a stipulated known covariance, not the package algorithm or empirical coverage.

sources.author: Kevin Sheppard and contributors
sources.version_date: Repository commit 13390eee49ea06fc42f831255ff2163f2ad13e8b; selected before cutoff; release equivalence unverified

primary_sources.version_date: Repository commit 13390eee49ea06fc42f831255ff2163f2ad13e8b; selected before cutoff; release equivalence unverified

inspected_anchors.inspected_text:
def diagnostics(self) -> DataFrame:
        """
        Post estimation diagnostics of first-stage fit

        Returns
        -------
        DataFrame
            DataFrame where each endogenous variable appears as a row and
            the columns contain alternative measures.  The columns are:

            * rsquared - R-squared from regression of endogenous on exogenous
              and instruments
            * partial.rsquared - R-squared from regression of the exogenous
              variable on instruments where both the exogenous variable and
              the instrument have been orthogonalized to the exogenous
              regressors in the model.
            * f.stat - Test that all coefficients are zero in the model
              used to estimate the partial R-squared. Uses a standard F-test
              when the covariance estimator is unadjusted - otherwise uses a
              Wald test statistic with a chi2 distribution.
            * f.pval - P-value of the test that all coefficients are zero
              in the model used to estimate the partial R-squared
            * f.dist - Distribution of f.stat
            * shea.rsquared - Shea's r-squared which measures the correlation
              between the projected and orthogonalized instrument on the
              orthogonalized endogenous regressor where the orthogonalization
              is with respect to the other included variables in the model.

for col in endog.pandas:
            # TODO: BUG in pandas-stube
            #  https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas-stubs/issues/97
            y = w * endog.pandas[[col]].to_numpy()
            ey = annihilate(y, x)
            partial = _OLS(ey, ez).fit(cov_type=self._cov_type, **self._cov_config)
            full = individual_results[str(col)]
            params = full.params.to_numpy()[-nz:]
            params = params[:, None]
            c = asarray(full.cov)[-nz:, -nz:]
            stat = params.T @ inv(c) @ params
            stat = float(stat.squeeze())
            if full.cov_type in ("homoskedastic", "unadjusted"):
                df_denom = full.df_resid
                stat /= params.shape[0]
            else:
                df_denom = None
            w_test = WaldTestStatistic(
                stat, null="", df=params.shape[0], df_denom=df_denom
            )

def anderson_rubin(self) -> InvalidTestStatistic | WaldTestStatistic:
        r"""
        Anderson-Rubin test of overidentifying restrictions

        Returns
        -------
        WaldTestStatistic
            Object containing test statistic, p-value, distribution and null

        Notes
        -----
        The Anderson-Rubin test examines whether the value of :math:`\kappa`
        computed for the LIML estimator is sufficiently close to one to
        indicate the model is not overidentified. The test statistic is

        .. math ::

          n \ln(\hat{\kappa}) \sim \chi^2_{q}

        where :math:`q = n_{instr} - n_{endog}`.
        """
        nobs, ninstr = self.model.instruments.shape
        nendog = self.model.endog.shape[1]
        name = "Anderson-Rubin test of overidentification"
        if ninstr - nendog == 0:
            return InvalidTestStatistic(
                "Test requires more instruments than endogenous variables.",
                name=name,
            )
        assert self._liml_kappa is not None
        stat = nobs * log(self._liml_kappa)
        df = ninstr - nendog
        null = "The model is not overidentified."
        return WaldTestStatistic(stat, null, df, name=name)

supported_claims: First-stage f.stat uses F for unadjusted covariance and chi-square Wald otherwise; preserve f.dist.
The anderson_rubin property tests overidentifying restrictions using LIML kappa and does not accept a coefficient-null value; do not route it as inversion for a weak-IV coefficient confidence set.
